name: Automatic renewal
why: You can be locked into another full term (and price increases) if you miss a narrow cancellation window.
fair_standard: Renewal only on affirmative opt-in, or month-to-month after the initial term, with a reminder at least 30 days before renewal and cancellation at any time with 30 days' notice.

name: One-sided right to change terms
why: The other party can change price, scope or rules after you sign, so the deal you agreed to is not the deal you get.
fair_standard: Material changes require at least 30 days' written notice and give you the right to terminate without penalty and receive a pro-rated refund.

name: Forced arbitration / class-action waiver
why: You give up the right to go to court or join with others; arbitration can be costly, private and favour repeat players.
fair_standard: Small-claims court carve-out, opt-out window of 30+ days, the drafting party pays arbitration fees, and a neutral venue near you.

name: Liability cap or waiver
why: If the other party causes you harm, your recovery may be capped at a trivial amount or excluded entirely.
fair_standard: Mutual caps of at least 12 months of fees, with carve-outs for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, data breaches and personal injury.

name: One-way indemnity
why: You may have to pay the other party's legal costs and damages, even for problems you did not cause.
fair_standard: Mutual indemnities limited to each party's own negligence or breach, capped, and with control of the defence.

name: Termination penalties or one-sided termination
why: Leaving early could cost you all remaining payments, while the other side may be able to walk away freely.
fair_standard: Termination rights on both sides, a capped fee (for example one month), and a duty on the other party to mitigate losses.

name: Late fees, penalties and hidden charges
why: Fees that compound or are not tied to real costs can quickly exceed the underlying amount owed.
fair_standard: A grace period of at least 5 days, a single fixed late fee no higher than about 5% of the payment, and all fees listed up front.

name: Security deposit terms
why: Vague deduction rules or long return windows make it easy to keep your deposit.
fair_standard: Return within the legal deadline (often 14 to 30 days) with an itemised list of deductions; normal wear and tear is never deductible.

name: Entry, access and monitoring
why: Broad access rights erode your privacy and quiet enjoyment.
fair_standard: At least 24 hours' written notice, reasonable hours, and stated purposes only, except in genuine emergencies.

name: Broad IP / content ownership grab
why: You may hand over ownership of, or unlimited rights to, your work, content or side projects.
fair_standard: Licence only what is needed to provide the service, revocable on termination; in employment, exclude prior inventions and work done on your own time and equipment.

name: Non-compete / non-solicit
why: This can stop you working in your field or region for a long time after the relationship ends.
fair_standard: Narrow scope and geography, 6 to 12 months at most, paid garden leave, and only where enforceable under local law.

name: Personal data use and sharing
why: Your data might be sold or shared for purposes unrelated to the service.
fair_standard: Use limited to providing the service, no sale of data, an opt-out for marketing, and deletion on request.

name: Distant venue / governing law
why: Disputes may have to be fought far away under unfamiliar law, which makes enforcing your rights impractical.
fair_standard: Your local law and courts, or at least a neutral venue.

name: Repair and maintenance burden
why: Shifting structural or appliance repairs onto you makes you pay for the owner's property.
fair_standard: The owner handles structural, plumbing, electrical, heating and appliance repairs; you pay only for damage beyond normal wear and tear.
